blocks.text: What you need before you start

content.text: A WordPress blog needs three things, and you can arrange all of them in one order. Get these ready first, and the install itself is the easy part.

items.text: A domain name.
This is your blog address. A .com costs Rs 2,999 for the first year and Rs 3,999 to renew, while a .pk costs Rs 4,999 for 2 years. Search for your name on the
domain search page
before you buy anything else.
A WordPress hosting plan.
This is where your blog lives.
WordPress hosting from Rs 1,499 per year
includes a one-click WordPress install, free SSL, free cPanel, daily backups and free migration, so a new blog needs nothing else to start.
An email address you actually read.
WordPress sends password resets, comments and update notices to your admin email. Use a mailbox you check every day, not one you open once a month.

blocks.text: Install WordPress with the one-click installer in cPanel

content.text: Every WordPress plan at ZedgeHost includes a one-click WordPress install inside cPanel. You do not upload files, create a database or touch any code. The installer does all of that for you.

items.text: Log in to cPanel.
Use the cPanel login details from your hosting welcome email. If you ordered hosting and a domain together, both are already connected.
Find the WordPress installer.
Use the search box at the top of cPanel and type WordPress, then open the installer. It is listed as a one-click WordPress install.
Choose your domain.
Pick the domain from the list. Leave the directory field empty, so your blog opens on your main address, for example yourdomain.com, and not in a subfolder.
Fill in the site details.
Enter a site name, a short tagline, an admin username, a strong password and your admin email. Do not use admin as the username, because it is the first name attackers try.
Click Install and wait.
The installer creates the database and the WordPress files for you. It usually finishes in a minute or two.
Log in at yourdomain.com/wp-admin.
Use the admin username and password you just set. This is your WordPress dashboard, where you write posts, change the theme and manage comments.

content.text: If you cannot find the installer in your cPanel, contact 24/7 support and they will point you to it. For the full picture of what happens between ordering and activation, see
how ordering works

blocks.text: First settings to change after installing WordPress

content.text: WordPress works out of the box, but five quick settings make your blog cleaner and easier to find. Do them before you publish your first post.

items.text: Set clean post links.
Go to Settings, then Permalinks, and choose Post Name. Your posts will then have readable addresses like yourdomain.com/your-post-title.
Set the timezone.
Go to Settings, then General, and set the timezone to Karachi (UTC+5), so your post times match Pakistan time.
Check the padlock.
Visit your site with https in front and look for the padlock in the browser. Free SSL is included in every plan, so a new blog should already show it.
Pick one simple theme.
Choose a light, simple theme and stick with it for now. You can change the design any time without losing your posts.
Write your first post.
Go to Posts, then Add New, write a short introduction post, and publish it. A live post shows you the whole flow, from writing to reading it on your own domain.

blocks.text: How much does it cost to start a WordPress blog in Pakistan?

content.text: The minimum first-year cost is a domain plus one year of hosting. A .com domain costs Rs 2,999 for the first year, and the WordPress Starter plan costs Rs 1,499 per year, so the total is Rs 4,498. With a .pk domain at Rs 4,999 for 2 years, the first payment is Rs 6,498. SSL, cPanel, daily backups and migration are included free, so there is nothing else to buy to get started.

blocks.text: WordPress hosting or shared hosting for a blog?

content.text: WordPress hosting uses the same four plans and prices as shared hosting, from Rs 1,499 to Rs 4,999 per year, with one-click WordPress installs. For a blog, WordPress hosting is the direct fit, because it is set up for WordPress from the start. Shared hosting works too, and it is the better pick if you plan to run a non-WordPress site later. See
shared hosting vs VPS hosting in Pakistan
for the full comparison, and
shared hosting from Rs 1,499 per year
for the shared plans.

blocks.text: 5 mistakes beginners make with a WordPress blog

content.text: The username admin is the first one attackers try, and WordPress does not let you change a username later. Pick a different admin username at install time, and use a long password you do not reuse anywhere else.

blocks.text: 2. Installing WordPress in a subfolder by accident

content.text: If you type blog into the directory field during install, your site opens at yourdomain.com/blog instead of yourdomain.com. Leave the directory field empty unless you deliberately want the blog in a folder. If you already installed it in a folder, reinstall it on the main address before you publish anything.

Visitors trust the padlock, and browsers warn about sites without it. Check that your site loads with https before you share your first post. Free SSL is included in every plan, so if the padlock is missing, contact support instead of publishing anyway.

A blog grows post by post, and losing it means losing months of work. Daily backups are included in every plan, so confirm they are running and know how to restore from one. Never rely on a single copy of your posts.

blocks.text: 5. Installing too many plugins at once

content.text: Each plugin adds load and another thing that can break or conflict. Start with only what you need, add one plugin at a time, and remove any you stop using. A new blog needs almost no plugins to publish its first posts.

blocks.text: After your first post: what next?

items.text: Publish on a schedule you can keep.
One good post a week beats ten rushed posts and then silence.
Set up categories.
A few clear categories help readers find related posts, and they keep your blog organised as it grows.
Check your blog on a phone.
Most readers in Pakistan will open your posts on a phone, so read your own post on one before you share it.
Keep WordPress updated.
Automatic WordPress core updates are included in every plan, so updates happen for you. Update your theme and plugins from the dashboard when WordPress tells you to.
